title: Remote state you can trust
scenario: "Audit wants proof that nobody can read or overwrite Terraform state with a storage key, and that we can roll back a corrupted state file." — Security & Compliance
mission: Prove the state backend is Entra-ID-only, versioned and locked, and practise recovering a previous state version.
objectives: Explain control plane vs data plane on Storage

prerequisites.notes: At least two applies of a layer so a state blob has more than one version.

cost: Cents — blob versions of small JSON files.

steps.title: Inspect the account
steps.detail: Read the storage account properties that matter: shared key access, versioning, public access.
steps.command: az storage account show -n <state_storage_account_name> --query "{sharedKey:allowSharedKeyAccess, public:allowBlobPublicAccess, tls:minimumTlsVersion}"

steps.title: List state blobs and versions
steps.detail: With --auth-mode login only. Find a layer with two or more versions.
steps.command: az storage blob list --account-name <sa> -c tfstate --auth-mode login --include v -o table

steps.title: See the lock
steps.detail: Start a plan of 10-foundation and, while it runs, look at the blob lease state in a second terminal.

steps.title: Explain recovery
steps.detail: Write down the exact steps to restore a previous version of 20-governance.tfstate (do not do it on a healthy state).

criteria.text: Shared key access is disabled on the state storage account
At least one state blob has two or more versions

expectedResult: You can show, with commands, that state access is identity-based and recoverable.
recovery: If listing fails with 403, your data-plane role is missing or still propagating (wait 5 minutes). Never enable shared keys to "fix" it.
dont: Do not enable shared key access
Do not restore a state version on a healthy layer
Do not edit state files by hand
hints: Being Owner gives you the control plane. What gives you the blobs?
Versioning and soft delete are properties of the blob service, not of the container.
az storage account blob-service-properties show -n <sa> shows isVersioningEnabled.

interview.question: Where does your Terraform state live, who can read it, and how would you recover a corrupted state?
followUps: How does locking work on Azure Storage?

debrief: State is the inventory mapping code to real resource IDs. Entra-only access (no shared keys) means every read/write is an auditable identity with a data-plane role. Versioning lets you promote a previous version to current; the blob lease is the lock that blocks concurrent applies.

checker.plan: Read-only: az storage account show (allowSharedKeyAccess), blob-service-properties (isVersioningEnabled), az storage blob list --auth-mode login --include v.
